Select a successful sync task.
Read the Task Details pane.

bugs.name: Canceled GeoJSON error persists in a new custom map dialog

Enter a temporary name and not-a-url, then click Load.
Cancel and reopen Add a map; the fields are blank but the previous error remains.

reviewedVariants.summary: A fresh Add a new map dialog retained the previously loaded world-map preview even though its name and GeoJSON URL fields were blank; the stale preview remained visible after settling.
reviewedVariants.expected: A newly opened dialog with a blank GeoJSON URL shows the empty preview state (“Load a GeoJSON file to see a preview”).
reviewedVariants.actual: After saving the QA map, reopening Add a map showed blank name and GeoJSON URL fields but still rendered the previously loaded world map. The mismatch remained visible after five seconds.
reproSteps: Open /admin/settings/maps while signed in as the authorized admin using the supplied saved session; no credentials were entered.
Click Add a map. Confirm the fresh dialog shows “Load a GeoJSON file to see a preview.”

Enter the unique QA map name “QA map preview reset 71c9f2” and GeoJSON URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/master/geojson/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.geojson, then click Load.
Select SOV_A3 as the region identifier property and ADMIN as the display-name property, then click Add map. Confirm the saved QA map appears and the success toast is shown.
Click Add a map again. Observe that the name and GeoJSON URL fields are blank while the previous world map remains in the preview pane; wait five seconds and confirm it remains visible.

bugs.name: General settings shows the Site URL help text under Redirect to HTTPS

Read the Site URL field description and the help text immediately below Redirect to HTTPS without changing any settings.
Observe that Redirect to HTTPS repeats the Site URL explanation rather than describing the toggle.

bugs.name: Database caching settings are clipped and policy choices unavailable in mobile layout

bugs.expected: The Database caching page should expose its cache-policy section and available choices, along with the related Pro information, in the 390×844 mobile viewport so an admin can inspect the settings.
bugs.actual: The secondary navigation occupies most of the viewport while the main pane is squeezed at the right edge. The title and explanatory copy are clipped or awkwardly wrapped, only a narrow slice of the Pro card is visible, and no cache-policy section or choices appear. The same layout returns after refresh.

Refresh once and inspect the same page again. The clipped layout persists and the policy choices remain unavailable in the viewport.

Navigate to /admin/tools/help.

Inspect the support and issue-report cards at the top of Help, then scroll the Help content to the expert-help and diagnostic-information sections. Observe that their text is confined to narrow columns and clipped at the viewport edge.

reviewedVariants.name: Cloud migration panel content is missing at mobile viewport
reviewedVariants.summary: At 390×844, Settings > Cloud renders only a narrow blank card with a diamond icon; the migration description and Learn more link remain unavailable after horizontal scrolling.
reviewedVariants.expected: The Cloud migration panel’s description and safe Learn more link should be visible and usable at 390×844, consistent with the same panel at wider viewports.

Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.

Wait for the page to settle. Observe that the Cloud heading and a narrow outlined card with only a diamond icon are visible, but no migration description or Learn more link appears.
Scroll horizontally across the page and then the Cloud panel. The card content remains absent. Do not activate the free-trial button or change settings.

reviewedVariants.name: Authentication Overview content is clipped by the settings sidebar at mobile viewport
reviewedVariants.summary: At 390×844, the Authentication Overview heading and provider card are clipped by the settings sidebar; horizontal scrolling does not make them readable.
reviewedVariants.expected: The Authentication Overview heading and provider-card content should be readable at 390×844, or reachable through normal scrolling/navigation without being obscured by the settings sidebar.

The heading and Google sign-in card are cut off at the right edge, leaving only a narrow sliver visible. Set the viewport to 390×844 before navigation and preserve the inherited Daytona warning header.
Navigate to /admin/settings/general.
Expand Authentication in the settings sidebar and select Overview; the resulting page is /admin/settings/authentication.

Observe the Authentication heading and Google sign-in provider card. Attempt horizontal scrolling in the main content area; do not activate setup controls or change authentication/provider configuration.
Wait five seconds and observe that the heading and card remain clipped.

reviewedVariants.name: Appearance upsell card content is clipped at mobile width
reviewedVariants.summary: At 390×844, the Appearance upsell renders as a narrow, clipped strip: after settling only its diamond icon is visible, and attempts to reveal the content expose only fragments. The exposed Learn more fragment does open the official Appearance documentation; no settings or trial flows were changed.
reviewedVariants.expected: At mobile width, the Appearance card should show its explanatory copy and Learn more destination within the visible page area, as it does at desktop and tablet widths.
reviewedVariants.actual: At 390×844, the settings sidebar occupies most of the viewport and the card is reduced to a narrow strip. Load the provided authorized signed-in administrator session; no credentials were entered.
Navigate to /admin/settings/whitelabel and wait for the page to settle.

Observe that the Appearance card appears as a narrow strip beside the wide settings sidebar, initially showing only its diamond icon. Try horizontal scrolling and locating the Learn more link; most card copy remains clipped, with only fragments exposed.

It opens https://www.metabase.com/docs/v0.58/configuring-metabase/appearance?utm_source=product&utm_medium=upsell&utm_campaign=whitelabel&utm_content=settings-appearance&source_plan=oss in a new tab. No settings or trial flow are changed.

reviewedVariants.name: LDAP settings content is unreadable beside the settings sidebar at mobile width
reviewedVariants.summary: At 390×844, the LDAP settings content stays compressed beside the settings sidebar: the host label and help text wrap almost one character per line, and the rest of the form is clipped.
reviewedVariants.expected: The LDAP settings page should let a signed-in administrator inspect its LDAP host label, help text, and adjacent form at 390×844; the page presents these as the information for the LDAP settings task.

Wait for the page to settle. Open and close the top-right menu, then attempt horizontal scrolling; observe that the settings sidebar remains and the LDAP content is still compressed and clipped.

reviewedVariants.name: Database cache policy controls are clipped at a 390×844 viewport
reviewedVariants.summary: The database caching settings are unusable at 390×844 without horizontal scrolling: the fixed sidebar leaves only a narrow strip of the form visible, and an Adaptive selection attempt leaves Don't cache results selected.
reviewedVariants.expected: The cache settings page presents its policy choices and controls so an administrator can select and configure the Adaptive policy at the specified viewport without horizontal scrolling. The page itself presents a cache-policy chooser and describes Adaptive as a policy.
reviewedVariants.actual: At 390×844, the sidebar extends to about x=257 and the main content begins around x=289, leaving roughly 101 px of the viewport for the form. The heading and policy content are cut off at the right edge, and Adaptive controls are not visibly reachable. Clicking the Adaptive option produced no visible change; a diagnostic check still showed Don't cache results selected. reproSteps: Load the supplied saved-auth state for a signed-in administrator; no credentials were used or changed.
At a 390×844 CSS-pixel viewport, open /admin/performance/databases.
Keep the viewport unchanged and do not scroll horizontally. Observe the cache heading and policy content clipped at the right edge.
Attempt to select the Adaptive policy. Observe that no visible selection or Adaptive controls appear and Don't cache results remains selected.
Try vertical scrolling and the top-bar menu as alternatives; neither reveals the clipped form. Wait for the page to settle and observe that the clipping persists. Do not save any settings.

reviewedVariants.name: Localization settings are clipped at a 390px viewport
reviewedVariants.summary: At 390×844, the Localization page's Number separator selector and its options are clipped; horizontal scrolling and waiting do not make the option labels fully readable.

reviewedVariants.name: Guest embedding card and New embed action are clipped at mobile width

reviewedVariants.name: Data permission detail pane is clipped at a 390px viewport, hiding permission controls

reviewedVariants.name: Collections permission editor clips group access controls at 390px viewport
reviewedVariants.summary: The Collections permissions editor keeps its tree and access table side by side at 390×844, leaving the selected group's access alternatives offscreen and unreachable.

bugs.name: Amazon Redshift and BigQuery labels overlap in the Add data dialog at 390 px
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, the Add data dialog renders Amazon Redshift and BigQuery labels colliding in the database connector list.
bugs.expected: In the database connector list, each connector name is readable in its own row, associated with that connector's icon.
bugs.actual: Amazon Redshift and BigQuery appear superimposed in the same row area, making those connector labels difficult to distinguish.

reviewedVariants.name: Mobile Add data connector choices overlap at 390×844
reviewedVariants.summary: On the 390×844 Add data modal, Amazon Redshift's label overlaps the BigQuery option, leaving the connector names visually ambiguous; the collision persists after reopening the modal and settling.
reviewedVariants.expected: Database connector names in the Add data chooser should remain visually distinct so a user can identify which database type they are choosing.

bugs.name: People table horizontal scrolling shifts the heading beneath the fixed sidebar at tablet width
bugs.summary: At 768×1024, horizontally scrolling the People table shifts the main content left beneath the fixed admin sidebar, clipping the People heading; scrolling left restores it.
bugs.expected: At 768×1024, horizontal scrolling the People table reveals its remaining columns without moving the People heading beneath the fixed admin sidebar.

Close the admin navigation menu and confirm Harbor Admin is visible in the People table.
Scroll horizontally right over the People table. Observe that additional row content is revealed while the People heading moves left beneath the fixed sidebar.
Scroll horizontally left and confirm the heading becomes fully visible again.

bugs.name: First Discard changes click does not reset invalid adaptive cache edit
bugs.summary: The first Discard changes click leaves the invalid Adaptive edit in place; repeating the same flow from the saved no-cache state reproduces it, and a second click is needed to reset the form.
bugs.expected: Clicking Discard changes once should abandon the unsaved Adaptive selection and invalid Multiplier value, returning the form to the saved “Don’t cache results” policy.
bugs.actual: After the first click, Adaptive remained selected, Multiplier remained 0, “Enter a positive number.” appeared, and Save changes was disabled. The state persisted after waiting five seconds. A second click on Discard changes returned the form to “Don’t cache results.”
reproSteps: Restore the supplied signed-in administrator session and navigate to /admin/performance/databases. No credentials were entered during this reproduction.
Confirm that “Don’t cache results” is selected as the saved state.
Select “Adaptive” without saving.
Enter 0 in the Multiplier field.
Click “Discard changes” once. Observe that Adaptive remains selected, Multiplier is 0, the positive-number validation message appears, and Save changes is disabled.
Wait five seconds and verify that the invalid edit remains; click “Discard changes” again and observe that the form returns to “Don’t cache results.”

bugs.name: Canceling Create user clears matching People search result
bugs.summary: Canceling Create user repeatedly removes the matching People search result while leaving the search query unchanged; reloading restores the row, and repeating the flow removes it again.
bugs.expected: After canceling the untouched Create user dialog, the People page should continue showing the Harbor Admin row for the unchanged “Harbor Admin” search.

reproSteps: Restore the authorized QA administrator’s signed-in session; no credentials were entered. Open /admin/people.
Enter “Harbor Admin” in the People search field and verify the Harbor Admin row appears.
Click “Invite someone” to open Create user. Do not enter any user details.
Open the Groups dropdown without selecting a group, then click Cancel.
Observe that the query remains “Harbor Admin” while the results area shows “No results found.”

bugs.name: Failed custom map save closes the editor and discards the draft
bugs.summary: Failed custom map save closes the editor and discards the draft.
bugs.expected: Reject the invalid URL while retaining the editor and entered map configuration so the URL can be corrected.
bugs.actual: Save a custom map with a URL the server rejects. The error toast shows, the editor closes, and reopening shows a blank draft. Editing an existing map loses unsaved edits too. Valid URL saves (control).
reproSteps: Use any reachable valid GeoJSON URL with polygon features and code/name properties. A test file is available in sandbox /tmp/MapQA-regions.geojson; get a fresh hosted download URL if needed.
As Admin, open Settings > Maps > Add a map.
Enter MapQA Regions and load a valid GeoJSON FeatureCollection with polygon features and code/name properties.
Select code as identifier and name as display name.
Replace URL with not-a-url and click Refresh; invalid GeoJSON file location appears in preview.
Click the still-enabled Add map button.

bugs.name: Changing a custom map's GeoJSON keeps stale property mappings and still saves
bugs.summary: Changing a custom map's GeoJSON keeps stale property mappings and still saves.
bugs.expected: Require valid identifier and display-name properties from the newly loaded file before saving, as required for initial custom map creation.
bugs.actual: Edit a saved custom map, change its URL to a GeoJSON with different property names, and Refresh. Both property pickers show "Select…" but Save map stays enabled and reports Changes saved. A fresh Add with nothing selected keeps Add disabled (control).
reproSteps: Own test files /tmp/MapQA-regions.geojson (code,name,population, two polygons) and /tmp/MapQA-alternate.geojson (id,label, triangle) are available in sandbox; generate fresh download URLs. Do not modify another worker's maps; use MapQA prefix.
Create a MapQA custom map using polygon GeoJSON with code/name/population properties and select valid identifier and display-name properties.
Reopen the map and replace its URL with GeoJSON containing only id and label properties, then click Refresh.
Observe both identifier and display-name selectors change to Select….
Without selecting replacement properties, click Save map.
Reload Maps and reopen the saved map.

bugs.name: Webhook Basic or Bearer auth saves untouched credential fields as literal undefined

reproSteps: As Admin create a fresh prefixed webhook with URL https://example.test/mo-email-webhook, a name and description, authentication None.

Save changes and reopen the same webhook.

Select the PeopleQA group in Groups, dismiss dropdown and click Update.
Observe the closed dialog and row still showing Default.

bugs.name: SMTP Clear leaves unsaved host, port and errors in the form

bugs.expected: Clicking Clear should reset all SMTP configuration form fields, clearing the host and port inputs and error messages.

bugs.name: Failed GeoJSON refresh keeps the previous file's properties and allows saving the rejected URL
bugs.summary: Failed GeoJSON refresh keeps the previous file's properties and allows saving the rejected URL.
bugs.expected: After rejected loading, property choices should not present unrelated properties from a previous GeoJSON file as options for the current file.
bugs.actual: In the custom map editor, load a valid GeoJSON, then refresh to a file that fails validation (missing properties, empty collection, or 404). reproSteps: Hover the table row and click its Hide table eye button. Reload and verify its Unhide table eye button remains in the tree.
Enter that table's display name in Search tables.

bugs.name: Undoing a saved field description fails with “Couldn't undo” and leaves the changed description
bugs.summary: Undoing a saved field description fails with “Couldn't undo” and leaves the changed description.
bugs.expected: Undo restores the previous empty description in both the field card and settings.
bugs.actual: Clicking Undo produced “Couldn't undo”; the field card and settings retained MO_META_UNDO_DESCRIPTION. The post-click assertion explicitly observed the error and retained text.
reproSteps: Record its original description; enter a unique temporary description such as MO_META_UNDO_DESCRIPTION.
Blur the description to save; observe the field card update and Description of Body updated notification.
Promptly click Undo in that notification.
Inspect the description in the field card and settings.

bugs.name: Saving 'Don't cache results' briefly shows '✓ Saved' but leaves Save changes and Discard changes buttons visible after entering an invalid Adaptive duration
bugs.summary: Saving 'Don't cache results' briefly shows '✓ Saved' but leaves Save changes and Discard changes buttons visible after entering an invalid Adaptive duration.
bugs.expected: Saving 'Don't cache results' should clear the dirty form state so that 'Save changes' and 'Discard changes' disappear, matching the clean saved state.
bugs.actual: After clicking 'Save changes', the button temporarily displays '✓ Saved' (00:41.200-00:45.800) but then reverts to 'Save changes' with 'Discard changes' still visible (00:46.000 onwards).
reproSteps: Open Admin > Performance > Database caching with Don't cache results saved.
Select Adaptive, enter -1 in Minimum query duration and blur to see Enter a positive number.
Switch to Don't cache results; Adaptive fields and error disappear.
Click enabled Save changes.

bugs.name: Revoking native access to last-selected database prevents switching to permitted databases
bugs.summary: Revoking native access to last-selected database prevents switching to permitted databases.
bugs.expected: When the last-selected database no longer permits native queries, select an eligible database or show a picker that lets the member select one.
bugs.actual: Fresh New → SQL query selects Sample Database as plain text with no picker, and Run/Refresh stays disabled even with SELECT 1 entered, although Release operations still allows native queries. Full navigation/reload does not fix it. Restoring Sample native access restores the picker showing both databases, and selecting Release operations succeeds. snapshots at 16:50:12 and 16:51:34; restored-working control at 16:52:32 and 16:52:34.
reproSteps: Use separate administrator and Maya (maya@example.test) browser sessions. Initially grant All Users Query builder and native access on both Sample Database and Release operations; Maya should have no additional groups granting Sample native access.

In the administrator session, open /admin/permissions, select All Users, and change Sample Database → Create queries to Query builder only. Save changes. Leave Release operations with Query builder and native access.
In Maya's session, navigate to a fresh page and open New → SQL query again.
Observe Sample Database remains selected as plain text, the database picker is absent, and typing SELECT 1 leaves Run/Refresh disabled, preventing selection of Release operations.
Reload and repeat New → SQL query to confirm persistence.

bugs.name: Setting 'Number of decimal places' to 101 is accepted without validation but renders preview values as integers
bugs.summary: Setting 'Number of decimal places' to 101 is accepted without validation but renders preview values as integers.
bugs.expected: Entering 101 in 'Number of decimal places' should be rejected with a validation error or format the preview values according to the decimal count, rather than formatting values with zero decimal places.
bugs.actual: The value 101 is accepted without error, and the Field preview renders price values as whole integers (29, 70, 35, 74, 83) instead of displaying decimals.
reproSteps: Use Products Price or equivalent numeric field. Original Price settings were Normal style with decimal count unset. Restore field settings after testing.
In Admin Table Metadata, expand Sample Database and select Products.
Open Price field settings by clicking the field card background, then open Preview.
Scroll field settings to Number of decimal places. Enter 101 and blur the field.
Observe the Table preview; reload and reopen Preview to check persistence.

bugs.name: Adaptive caching caches ~2s saved query despite 3-second minimum query duration
bugs.summary: Adaptive caching caches ~2s saved query despite 3-second minimum query duration.
bugs.expected: The admin copy says "Metabase will cache all saved questions with an average query execution time greater than this many seconds". A query that averages about 2.0s should not be cached when the minimum is 3 seconds, so every reload should run it again and show a new timestamp.
bugs.actual: A new saved question whose runs take about 2.0s showed the same timestamp after two reloads, and the bottom-right indicator showed the tooltip "Showing cached results from a few seconds ago".
reproSteps: As an admin, open Admin > Performance and set the default caching policy to Adaptive with a Minimum query duration of 3 seconds. Save.
Click Exit admin, then New > SQL query, and choose the Release operations database.
Enter SELECT to_char(clock_timestamp(), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.MS') AS mo_verify_at, pg_sleep(2) AS performance_delay and run it. It takes about 2.0s.
Save it as a new question.
Reload the page and note the timestamp. Reload again and hover over the bottom-right execution indicator.
Observe the same timestamp and the tooltip 'Showing cached results from a few seconds ago'.

bugs.name: Saving an existing segment with a three-space name silently leaves the editor open without validation feedback
bugs.summary: Saving an existing segment with a three-space name silently leaves the editor open without validation feedback.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only name is rejected with understandable validation feedback or saving is disabled, as it is for an empty name.
bugs.actual: Save changes is enabled for three spaces. Clicking it leaves the editor open with blank-looking name and no error, validation or success message.
reproSteps: As admin open Table Metadata > Segments > New segment.
Select Sample Database > Orders and add Total between 100 and 200 filter.
Enter a unique descriptive segment name and description; Save changes.
Open the created segment using its name or Actions > Edit Segment.
Replace name with exactly three spaces and enter a reason for changes (tested: QA blank name validation).
Click enabled Save changes and inspect the settled page.

bugs.name: Renaming an API key to an existing key's name exposes raw SQL constraint error
bugs.summary: Renaming an API key to an existing key's name exposes raw SQL constraint error.
bugs.expected: Reject the duplicate name with understandable validation, like the create dialog's 'An API key with this name already exists', and retain the editor for correction.
bugs.actual: Edit dialog displays 'Unique index or primary key violation' followed by PUBLIC.CONSTRAINT_FB_INDEX_5, PUBLIC.API_KEY(NAME NULLS FIRST), and SQL UPDATE statement details. Save shows Failed.
reproSteps: As an admin open Authentication > API keys.
Create two disposable API keys with distinct unique names (for example Mo-auth-edge-<unique suffix> and Mo-auth-boundary-<unique suffix>), both in All Users. Close each one-time key dialog.
Edit the second key using its pencil icon.
Replace its name with the first key's exact existing name and click Save.

bugs.name: Editing an API key permits a whitespace-only name and persists an unnamed list row
bugs.summary: Editing an API key permits a whitespace-only name and persists an unnamed list row.
bugs.expected: Reject whitespace-only names, consistent with Create's 'Value must be a non-blank string' validation; preserve the existing identifiable name.
bugs.actual: Save succeeds and the key list renders a blank-name row. After refresh, reopening the editor displays a blank/whitespace Key name field.
reproSteps: As admin open Authentication > API keys.
Create a disposable uniquely named key in All Users and close its one-time key dialog.
Open its pencil editor and replace Key name with three spaces.
Click Save; inspect the API key list.
Refresh and reopen the row's pencil editor.

bugs.name: Custom map rejects reachable valid GeoJSON URL containing an encoded plus in its query signature
bugs.summary: Custom map rejects reachable valid GeoJSON URL containing an encoded plus in its query signature.
bugs.expected: Entering a reachable URL serving valid GeoJSON should load the map preview upon clicking Refresh.
bugs.actual: After entering the signed URL containing '%2B' and clicking Refresh, Metabase displays 'GeoJSON URL failed to load' instead of loading the map preview.
reproSteps: As Admin, open Settings > Maps and add or edit a uniquely named custom map.
Host a valid GeoJSON FeatureCollection containing one polygon and region_id/region_label string properties at a signed URL whose signature contains %2B.
Enter that URL in GeoJSON URL and click Load or Refresh.
Compare with the same file at a fresh signed URL without %2B; this renders successfully.
Open the rejected URL directly in a browser tab to verify valid GeoJSON is served, then return and refresh the rejected URL again.

bugs.name: Spark SQL connection string prefills Host but ignores Port=10001
bugs.summary: Spark SQL connection string prefills Host but ignores Port=10001.
bugs.expected: Entering a connection string specifying Port=10001 should prefill 10001 into the Port field.
bugs.actual: Host is prefilled with localhost, but the Port field remains empty with the placeholder 10000.
reproSteps: In Admin Databases open Add database and select Spark SQL.
Enter jdbc:sparksql:Server=localhost;Port=10001;Database=mo_qa into Connection string (optional).
Blur and inspect Host and Port.

bugs.name: Page URL link text setting does not update table preview labels
bugs.summary: Page URL link text setting does not update table preview labels.
bugs.expected: With Display as Link selected, setting Link text to Open QA page should label the preview links Open QA page.
bugs.actual: Link text input shows Open QA page, but all five preview rows still show www.piespace.example URLs (invite, home, home, invite, pies).
reproSteps: Open Admin Table Metadata and expand Sample Database.
Select Analytic Events, then Page URL (URL semantic type). Record original empty Link text for restoration.
Open Preview, keep Table tab selected and scroll field settings to Display as Link.
Enter Open QA page in Link text and blur the field.
Inspect all five table preview rows after waiting for the change.

bugs.name: Segment editor shows singular result count as “1 rows”
bugs.summary: Segment editor shows singular result count as “1 rows”.
bugs.expected: A single matching row is labeled “1 row.”
bugs.actual: The editor displays “1 rows.”
reproSteps: Open an Admin segment matching exactly one row.
Read the result count beside Preview.

bugs.name: Product ID Search box filtering preview gives no suggestions for remapped title "Rustic"
bugs.summary: Product ID Search box filtering preview gives no suggestions for remapped title "Rustic".
bugs.expected: With Filtering set to Search box on a foreign key whose display values use the foreign key's Title, typing "Rustic" in the preview should search the Title values and suggest "Rustic Paper Wallet" so it can be selected.
bugs.actual: The input shows "Rustic" (its empty placeholder is "Enter an ID"), but no dropdown or suggestion appears after waiting and clicking into the input. The network log shows no field search or values request after typing, only an unrelated /api/dataset call.
reproSteps: Sign in as an admin and open /admin/datamodel.
Select Sample Database > Reviews > Product ID (URL .../admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/4/field/65).
Confirm Semantic type is Foreign Key → Products → ID and Display values is Use foreign key > Title. The original Filtering value is Plain input box.
Set Filtering to Search box.
Click Preview, then the Filtering tab (the Table tab lists 'Rustic Paper Wallet' values).
Type 'Rustic' into the Filter value input, click it, and wait 4 seconds: no suggestions appear.
Afterwards I set Filtering back to Plain input box.

bugs.name: Unhidden tables remain missing from the segment table picker until reload
bugs.summary: Unhidden tables remain missing from the segment table picker until reload.
bugs.expected: Unhiding a table should make it immediately available in the segment table picker.
bugs.actual: Reviews is correctly excluded while hidden. After clicking Unhide table, a success toast appears and the sidebar now offers Hide table, confirming it is visible. Reopening Select a table > Sample Database still omits Reviews. Full reload restores Reviews in the picker. Reproduced twice.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture admin. Open Admin > Table Metadata > Sample Database > Reviews (or /admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/4). Start with Reviews visible.
Hide Reviews using its sidebar eye control, then open Segments > New segment > Select a table > Sample Database. Confirm Reviews is absent and close the table picker.
Without reloading, use the Reviews sidebar crossed-eye control to Unhide table. Confirm success and that the sidebar now offers Hide table.
Open Select a table > Sample Database again. Reviews is still absent even though it is now visible.
Reload the create-segment page, reopen the table picker and select Sample Database. Reviews is now present.

bugs.name: PostgreSQL JDBC connection-string prefill omits the user query parameter from Username
bugs.summary: PostgreSQL JDBC connection-string prefill omits the user query parameter from Username.
bugs.expected: The JDBC connection string should prefill Username as qa_user along with its other supplied connection details, consistent with the visible instruction that a connection string pre-fills the details below.
bugs.actual: Host invalid.example.test, port 5432, database name qa_connection and SSL are prefilled, but Username remains empty with the username placeholder.
reproSteps: As Admin open Databases, then Add database with default PostgreSQL type.
Enter jdbc:postgresql://invalid.example.test:5432/qa_connection?user=qa_user&password=qa_password&ssl=true in Connection string (optional).
Blur the textarea and inspect the prefilled fields.

bugs.name: Changing a field with Normal style to Currency semantic type hides the Style selector while leaving plain-number formatting in previews
bugs.summary: Changing a field with Normal style to Currency semantic type hides the Style selector while leaving plain-number formatting in previews.
bugs.expected: Selecting Currency semantic type should apply currency formatting or retain the Style selector so currency styling can be enabled.
bugs.actual: The Style dropdown disappears from the field formatting pane, leaving previously set Normal styling active so that Table and Detail previews display plain numbers (4.6) with no currency unit or symbol.
reproSteps: As admin open Sample Database Products table, Rating field.
While semantic type is Score, explicitly choose Normal in number Style settings.
Change semantic type to Currency; reload and verify it persists.
Select Euro in currency selector under Semantic type and open Preview.
Inspect Table and Detail previews, then scroll through formatting settings.
